eyebrow: APIs & JSON for AI Applications · Chapter 1, Lesson 2
subtitle: The architectural style behind most APIs you'll ever call

steps.label: Resources
steps.sub: nouns, not actions — each addressed by its own URL

steps.label: Stateless
steps.sub: every request carries everything the server needs

steps.label: Standard verbs
steps.sub: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE — not custom names

code:
GET  /users/42          -> the user with id 42
GET  /orders/1001       -> order number 1001
POST /messages          -> create a new message

Older style:
POST /getUserById?id=42
caption: The resource lives in the URL; the verb says what to do to it.

steps.label: Every request
steps.sub: carries its own auth token, every single time

steps.label: No server memory
steps.sub: the server recalls nothing about your last call

steps.label: Any server, any call
steps.sub: nothing is "sticky" to one particular machine

subtitle: The verbs REST reuses, and what the server's answer means
